notes:
The bare numbers are map numbers from each year's West Coast of Scotland station list. The two reports number them differently. 1883 list (sources/ia/1883_reportonmigratio51883harv_djvu.txt:3776-3835): 81 Cape Wrath, 82 Rhu Stoir, 83 Butt, 84 Stornoway, 85 Island Glass, 86 Monach, 87 Ushenish, 88 Barra Head, 89 Rona, 90 Kyleakin, 91 Isle Ornsay, 92 Ardnamurchan, 93 Hynish, 94 Skerryvore, 95 Dhuheartach, 96 Sound of Mull, 97 Corran, 98 Lismore, 99 Fladda, 100 Rhuvaal, 101 M'Arthur's Head, 102 Skervuile, 103 Rhinns of Islay, 104 Lochindaul, 105 Kintyre, 107 Devaar, 108 Pladda, 109 Lamlash, 110 Turnberry, 111 Corsewall, 112 Loch Ryan, 113 Portpatrick, 114 Mull of Galloway, 115 Little Ross. 1885 list (sources/gutenberg/1885_pg65840.txt:3980-4020): the same through 92, then 93 Skerryvore+Hynish, 94 Dhuheartach, 95 Sound of Mull, 96 Corran, 97 Lismore, 98 Fladda, 99 Rhuvaal, 100 M'Arthur's, 101 Skervuile, 102 Rhinns, 103 Lochindaul, 104 Kintyre, 105 Sanda, 106 Devaar, 107 Pladda, 108 Lamlash, 109 Turnberry, 109B Ailsa Craig, 110 Corsewall, 111 Loch Ryan, 112 Portpatrick, 113 Mull of Galloway, 114 Little Ross. As a check, the 1885 sentence 'five stations--102, 108, 109, 110, 113' names only stations that sent returns that year under the 1885 numbering.

CHECK FIRST: four items carry both 1883 and 1885 uses but stand for different stations in each year. They can't be resolved as single items; split them by year. I gave the 1883 meaning: n=0 '101' (1883 mcarthurs-head / 1885 skervuile), n=1 '102' (1883 skervuile / 1885 rhinns-of-islay), n=4 '109' (1883 holy-isle / 1885 turnberry), n=43 '98' (1883 lismore / 1885 fladda). Fladda sent no 1885 return, so check any 1885 '98' in the text. '86' and '90' are the same in both years and need no split.

Other things to check: n=651/652 Isle of Man treated as all the Manx stations; including Bahama Bank L.V. is my guess, and '(R. Clyne)' may name a single station. n=995 'Pentland' (Pentland Skerries, an East Coast station) turns up in a 1883 West Coast table. n=1208 'Start Point' read as Orkney, not Devon. n=1292 'Tyree' (1879) read as the Hynish station, not a Tiree correspondent. n=372 Erraid (Dubh Artach's shore station) kept as a place. n=701 Kyleakin Ferry read as the Kyleakin light. n=782/783 Loch Indaal: the light, not the loch. n=648 Islay kept as a place (four stations on the island). n=302 'Douglas' (1881) read as Douglas Head. Uncertain place identifications: Castletown (Isle of Man vs Caithness), Kincardine (on Forth?), Glenbervie (Larbert, not Kincardineshire), Horsley (which one), 'Rosely Castle' (Rose Castle or Rosley, Cumberland), Priory Farm (not identified), Douglas Hall (Kirkcudbrightshire assumed), Ballina (Mayo assumed). I classed positions at sea (miles from land, lat./long., Mid-Atlantic) as place 'North Atlantic Ocean'; reclass them as none if you prefer. The barque 'East' is none.
